correctness.rationale: The proof uses the finite Abrams model after checking its subdivision hypotheses on the cubic girth-six Heawood graph. The bundled verifier reconstructs all 182 zero-cells, 504 one-cells, and 336 two-cells; checks every two-cell satisfies the chain identity; and computes exact mod-2 boundary ranks 181 and 307 by bit-vector Gaussian elimination. Thus the reduced Betti ranks are 16 and 29 in degrees 1 and 2, with no cells above degree 2. The verifier and certificate hashes are recorded in the package.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical Fano-plane Levi graph and the smallest cubic cage of girth six, so it is a natural rather than arbitrary test object for graph configuration topology. The exact nonzero second-homology rank 29 and first-homology rank 16 provide a reusable benchmark for deletion/contraction calculations, graph braid groups, and comparisons of highly symmetric incidence graphs; these ranks are not forced by the general literature framework or by the cell counts alone.
